import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.4

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

A loop is a set with a binary operation `*`, a two-sided identity `1`, and unique left and
right division; the *loop signature* is `(*, ⧵, /, 1)`, in which loops form a variety.
The *laws* of a loop $L$ are the identities `s ≈ t` between terms of this signature that hold
under every assignment of the variables in $L$. The laws of $L$ have a *finite basis* if some
finite set of identities has exactly the laws of $L$ as its equational consequences (in the
class of all algebras of the loop signature; since loops are defined by finitely many
identities, restricting to loops gives the same notion).
"Nilpotent" is Bruck's central nilpotency: the upper central series
$1 = Z_0 \le Z_1 \le Z_2 \le \dots$, with $Z_{n+1}/Z_n = Z(L/Z_n)$, reaches $L$ after
finitely many steps. By the Oates–Powell theorem every finite group has a finite basis for
its laws; the problem asks for a finite nilpotent loop showing that the loop analogue fails.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

class LoopSignature (α : Type*) extends Mul α, One α, Div α where
  /-- Left division: in a loop, `a ⧵ b` is the solution `x` of `a * x = b`. -/
  ldiv : α → α → α
blocks.docstring:
An algebra in the signature of loops: a multiplication `*`, a constant `1`, a left
division `⧵` and a right division `/`. No axioms are imposed.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib Mul/One/Div classes (used as parents); the EquationalTheories file's bespoke `Magma` (single binary operation only, no divisions/identity).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».LoopSignature
justification.why_needed: Algebras of the loop signature (*, ⧵, /, 1) without axioms; needed as the class of models over which equational consequence is evaluated.

blocks.name: LoopSignature
blocks.text:
/-- An algebra in the signature of loops: a multiplication `*`, a constant `1`, a left
division `⧵` and a right division `/`. No axioms are imposed. -/
class LoopSignature (α : Type*) extends Mul α, One α, Div α where
  /-- Left division: in a loop, `a ⧵ b` is the solution `x` of `a * x = b`. -/
  ldiv : α → α → α
@[inherit_doc] local infixl:70 " ⧵ " => LoopSignature.ldiv

blocks.code:
class Loop (α : Type*) extends LoopSignature α where
  one_mul : ∀ a : α, 1 * a = a
  mul_one : ∀ a : α, a * 1 = a
  mul_ldiv : ∀ a b : α, a * (a ⧵ b) = b
  ldiv_mul : ∀ a b : α, a ⧵ (a * b) = b
  rdiv_mul : ∀ a b : α, (a / b) * b = a
  mul_rdiv : ∀ a b : α, (a * b) / b = a
blocks.docstring:
A loop: an algebra `(L, *, ⧵, /, 1)` in the loop signature in which `1` is a two-sided
identity, `a ⧵ b` is the unique solution `x` of `a * x = b`, and `a / b` is the unique
solution `y` of `y * b = a`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `Group`/`MulOneClass`/`IsCancelMul` — none captures non-associative loops with division operations.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».Loop
justification.why_needed: Loops (identity + unique left/right division, given by the standard quasigroup identities). Mathlib has no quasigroup or loop structure (only Matroid.IsLoop, unrelated).

class Loop (α : Type*) extends LoopSignature α where

def LoopTerm.eval {α : Type*} [LoopSignature α] (v : ℕ → α) : LoopTerm → α
  | var n => v n
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | ldiv s t => s.eval v ⧵ t.eval v
  | rdiv s t => s.eval v / t.eval v
blocks.docstring:
The value of a term in an algebra `α` of the loop signature under an assignment `v` of the
variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `FreeMagma` (only one binary operation, no constant or division symbols); `FirstOrder.Language.Term` (heavier model-theoretic machinery; no ready loop language).

/-- A law (identity) in the loop signature is a pair of terms `(s, t)`, read as `s ≈ t`. -/
abbrev LoopLaw := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

blocks.code:
def LoopSignature.Satisfies (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → α, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v
blocks.docstring:
The algebra `α` satisfies the law `s ≈ t` if `s` and `t` take the same value under every
assignment of the variables in `α`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or the repo about varieties/equational theories/finitely based laws.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».LoopSignature.Satisfies, LoopSignature.laws, LoopLaw.IsConsequence, LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of an identity, the set of laws of an algebra, semantic equational consequence over all algebras of the signature (in Type; sufficient by Birkhoff's completeness theorem), and the finite-basis property (a finite set whose consequences are exactly the laws).

blocks.name: LoopSignature.Satisfies
blocks.text:
/-- The algebra `α` satisfies the law `s ≈ t` if `s` and `t` take the same value under every
assignment of the variables in `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.Satisfies (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → α, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

blocks.code:
def LoopSignature.laws (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Set LoopLaw :=
  {e | LoopSignature.Satisfies α e}
blocks.docstring: The laws of `α`: the set of all identities in the loop signature holding in `α`.

blocks.name: LoopSignature.laws

blocks.docstring:
The law `e` is an equational consequence of the set of laws `S`: every algebra of the loop
signature satisfying all laws in `S` satisfies `e`. By Birkhoff's completeness theorem this
agrees with derivability of `e` from `S` in equational logic.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or the repo about varieties/equational theories/finitely based laws.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».LoopSignature.Satisfies, LoopSignature.laws, LoopLaw.IsConsequence, LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of an identity, the set of laws of an algebra, semantic equational consequence over all algebras of the signature (in Type; sufficient by Birkhoff's completeness theorem), and the finite-basis property (a finite set whose consequences are exactly the laws).

blocks.name: LoopLaw.IsConsequence
blocks.text:
/-- The law `e` is an equational consequence of the set of laws `S`: every algebra of the loop
signature satisfying all laws in `S` satisfies `e`. By Birkhoff's completeness theorem this
agrees with derivability of `e` from `S` in equational logic. -/
def LoopLaw.IsConsequence (S : Set LoopLaw) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ (β : Type) [LoopSignature β], (∀ e' ∈ S, LoopSignature.Satisfies β e') →
    LoopSignature.Satisfies β e

blocks.code:
def LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set LoopLaw, S.Finite ∧ ∀ e, LoopLaw.IsConsequence S e ↔ e ∈ LoopSignature.laws α
blocks.docstring:
The laws of `α` have a finite basis: there is a finite set `S` of laws whose equational
consequences are exactly the laws of `α`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or the repo about varieties/equational theories/finitely based laws.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».LoopSignature.Satisfies, LoopSignature.laws, LoopLaw.IsConsequence, LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of an identity, the set of laws of an algebra, semantic equational consequence over all algebras of the signature (in Type; sufficient by Birkhoff's completeness theorem), and the finite-basis property (a finite set whose consequences are exactly the laws).

blocks.name: LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis
blocks.text:
/-- The laws of `α` have a finite basis: there is a finite set `S` of laws whose equational
consequences are exactly the laws of `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set LoopLaw, S.Finite ∧ ∀ e, LoopLaw.IsConsequence S e ↔ e ∈ LoopSignature.laws α

blocks.code:
def CongrMod (N : Set L) (a b : L) : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ N, a = b * n
blocks.docstring:
`a` is congruent to `b` modulo the subset `N`, i.e. `a ∈ b * N`. When `N` is a normal
subloop this says that `a` and `b` have the same image in the quotient loop `L / N`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `upperCentralSeries`/`Group.IsNilpotent`/`Subgroup.center` — group-only, cannot be applied to loops.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».Loop.CongrMod, Loop.centerMod, Loop.center, Loop.upperCentralSeries, Loop.IsCentrallyNilpotent
justification.why_needed: Bruck's central nilpotency for loops: centre (nucleus ∩ commutant), upper central series with Z_{n+1}/Z_n = Z(L/Z_n) expressed without quotient loops via coset congruence a ∈ bN, and nilpotency as the series reaching L.

blocks.name: CongrMod
blocks.text:
/-- `a` is congruent to `b` modulo the subset `N`, i.e. `a ∈ b * N`. When `N` is a normal
subloop this says that `a` and `b` have the same image in the quotient loop `L / N`. -/
def CongrMod (N : Set L) (a b : L) : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ N, a = b * n

blocks.docstring:
The centre of `L` modulo `N`: the elements that commute and associate (in every position)
with all elements of `L` modulo `N`. When `N` is a normal subloop this is the preimage of the
centre `Z(L / N)` of the quotient loop under the quotient map `L → L / N`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `upperCentralSeries`/`Group.IsNilpotent`/`Subgroup.center` — group-only, cannot be applied to loops.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.4».Loop.CongrMod, Loop.centerMod, Loop.center, Loop.upperCentralSeries, Loop.IsCentrallyNilpotent
justification.why_needed: Bruck's central nilpotency for loops: centre (nucleus ∩ commutant), upper central series with Z_{n+1}/Z_n = Z(L/Z_n) expressed without quotient loops via coset congruence a ∈ bN, and nilpotency as the series reaching L.

blocks.name: centerMod
blocks.text:
/-- The centre of `L` modulo `N`: the elements that commute and associate (in every position)
with all elements of `L` modulo `N`. When `N` is a normal subloop this is the preimage of the
centre `Z(L / N)` of the quotient loop under the quotient map `L → L / N`. -/
def centerMod (N : Set L) : Set L :=
  {a | ∀ x y : L, CongrMod N (a * x) (x * a) ∧
    CongrMod N (a * x * y) (a * (x * y)) ∧
    CongrMod N (x * a * y) (x * (a * y)) ∧
    CongrMod N (x * y * a) (x * (y * a))}

blocks.docstring:
The centre of the loop `L`: the elements that commute with every element and associate
with every pair of elements in every position, i.e. the intersection of the nucleus with the
commutant.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `upperCentralSeries`/`Group.IsNilpotent`/`Subgroup.center` — group-only, cannot be applied to loops.

blocks.name: upperCentralSeries
blocks.text:
/-- The upper central series of the loop `L`: `Z₀ = {1}` and `Z_{n+1} / Z_n = Z(L / Z_n)`. -/
def upperCentralSeries (L : Type*) [Loop L] : ℕ → Set L
  | 0 => {1}
  | n + 1 => centerMod (upperCentralSeries L n)

blocks.code:
def IsCentrallyNilpotent (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, upperCentralSeries L n = Set.univ
blocks.docstring:
A loop is centrally nilpotent (in the sense of Bruck) if its upper central series reaches
the whole loop after finitely many steps.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `upperCentralSeries`/`Group.IsNilpotent`/`Subgroup.center` — group-only, cannot be applied to loops.

theorem congrMod_singleton_one (a b : L) : CongrMod {1} a b ↔ a = b := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl, rfl⟩
    exact Loop.mul_one b
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨1, rfl, (Loop.mul_one a).symm⟩
blocks.docstring: Congruence modulo the trivial subloop is equality.

theorem congrMod_singleton_one (a b : L) : CongrMod {1} a b ↔ a = b := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl, rfl⟩
    exact Loop.mul_one b
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨1, rfl, (Loop.mul_one a).symm⟩

  ext a
  simp [upperCentralSeries, centerMod, center, congrMod_singleton_one]

blocks.docstring:
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

That is, there is a finite loop $L$ which is centrally nilpotent (its upper central series
reaches $L$) and whose laws, i.e. the identities in the loop signature `(*, ⧵, /, 1)` holding
in $L$, are not the equational consequences of any finite set of identities.

blocks.text:
/--
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

That is, there is a finite loop $L$ which is centrally nilpotent (its upper central series
reaches $L$) and whose laws, i.e. the identities in the loop signature `(*, ⧵, /, 1)` holding
in $L$, are not the equational consequences of any finite set of identities.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.4» :
    ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Loop L), Finite L ∧ Loop.IsCentrallyNilpotent L ∧
      ¬ LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis L := by
  sorry
end Kourovka.«8.4»

claims.decomposer_note: Imperative 'construct' is an existence question: ∃ a loop L (with identity element and left/right division) that is finite and centrally nilpotent (upper central series reaches L in finitely many steps) such that the set of identities (laws, in the loop signature) holding in L is not finitely based, i.e. no finite set of identities of L has all identities of L as equational consequences — the loop analogue of the failure of the Oates–Powell theorem; 'nilpotent' must be read as Bruck's central nilpotency for loops, not as a group-theoretic notion.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematically faithful content (∃ finite loop in the equational signature (1,·,\,/), Bruck-centrally nilpotent, whose equational theory has no finite basis); none is wrong. c03 was chosen as the base for quality: Mathlib-style classes with `*`, `1`, `/` notation, a clean separation between arbitrary algebras of the loop signature (`LoopSignature`) and loops, the textbook definition of a finite basis (a finite set whose equational consequences are exactly the laws of L — this forces S ⊆ laws L), Bruck's upper central series stated literally (Z₀ = {1}, Z_{n+1} = preimage of Z(L/Z_n), expressed via cosets a ∈ bN, which is the congruence of the normal subloop Z_n), API lemmas checking Z₁ = centre and that congruence mod {1} is equality, no lines over 100 chars, and a thorough module docstring. I added a `Loop Unit` instance and two `@[category test]` sanity checks (trivial loop is nilpotent and finitely based, adapted from c05) to cover the bespoke `HasFiniteBasis`/`IsCentrallyNilpotent` definitions. Verified with `lake --wfail build` under the repo's linters: only the expected sorry.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.4

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

A loop is a set with a binary operation `*`, a two-sided identity `1`, and unique left and
right division; the *loop signature* is `(*, ⧵, /, 1)`, in which loops form a variety.
The *laws* of a loop $L$ are the identities `s ≈ t` between terms of this signature that hold
under every assignment of the variables in $L$. The laws of $L$ have a *finite basis* if some
finite set of identities has exactly the laws of $L$ as its equational consequences (in the
class of all algebras of the loop signature; since loops are defined by finitely many
identities, restricting to loops gives the same notion).
"Nilpotent" is Bruck's central nilpotency: the upper central series
$1 = Z_0 \le Z_1 \le Z_2 \le \dots$, with $Z_{n+1}/Z_n = Z(L/Z_n)$, reaches $L$ after
finitely many steps. By the Oates–Powell theorem every finite group has a finite basis for
its laws; the problem asks for a finite nilpotent loop showing that the loop analogue fails.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

/-- An algebra in the signature of loops: a multiplication `*`, a constant `1`, a left
division `⧵` and a right division `/`. No axioms are imposed. -/
class LoopSignature (α : Type*) extends Mul α, One α, Div α where
  /-- Left division: in a loop, `a ⧵ b` is the solution `x` of `a * x = b`. -/
  ldiv : α → α → α

@[inherit_doc] local infixl:70 " ⧵ " => LoopSignature.ldiv

/-- A loop: an algebra `(L, *, ⧵, /, 1)` in the loop signature in which `1` is a two-sided
identity, `a ⧵ b` is the unique solution `x` of `a * x = b`, and `a / b` is the unique
solution `y` of `y * b = a`. -/
class Loop (α : Type*) extends LoopSignature α where
  one_mul : ∀ a : α, 1 * a = a
  mul_one : ∀ a : α, a * 1 = a
  mul_ldiv : ∀ a b : α, a * (a ⧵ b) = b
  ldiv_mul : ∀ a b : α, a ⧵ (a * b) = b
  rdiv_mul : ∀ a b : α, (a / b) * b = a
  mul_rdiv : ∀ a b : α, (a * b) / b = a

/-- Terms in the signature of loops, with variables indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LoopTerm
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm

/-- The value of a term in an algebra `α` of the loop signature under an assignment `v` of the
variables. -/
def LoopTerm.eval {α : Type*} [LoopSignature α] (v : ℕ → α) : LoopTerm → α
  | var n => v n
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | ldiv s t => s.eval v ⧵ t.eval v
  | rdiv s t => s.eval v / t.eval v

/-- A law (identity) in the loop signature is a pair of terms `(s, t)`, read as `s ≈ t`. -/
abbrev LoopLaw := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

/-- The algebra `α` satisfies the law `s ≈ t` if `s` and `t` take the same value under every
assignment of the variables in `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.Satisfies (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → α, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

/-- The laws of `α`: the set of all identities in the loop signature holding in `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.laws (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Set LoopLaw :=
  {e | LoopSignature.Satisfies α e}

/-- The law `e` is an equational consequence of the set of laws `S`: every algebra of the loop
signature satisfying all laws in `S` satisfies `e`. By Birkhoff's completeness theorem this
agrees with derivability of `e` from `S` in equational logic. -/
def LoopLaw.IsConsequence (S : Set LoopLaw) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ (β : Type) [LoopSignature β], (∀ e' ∈ S, LoopSignature.Satisfies β e') →
    LoopSignature.Satisfies β e

/-- The laws of `α` have a finite basis: there is a finite set `S` of laws whose equational
consequences are exactly the laws of `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set LoopLaw, S.Finite ∧ ∀ e, LoopLaw.IsConsequence S e ↔ e ∈ LoopSignature.laws α

namespace Loop

variable {L : Type*} [Loop L]

/-- `a` is congruent to `b` modulo the subset `N`, i.e. `a ∈ b * N`. When `N` is a normal
subloop this says that `a` and `b` have the same image in the quotient loop `L / N`. -/
def CongrMod (N : Set L) (a b : L) : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ N, a = b * n

/-- The centre of `L` modulo `N`: the elements that commute and associate (in every position)
with all elements of `L` modulo `N`. When `N` is a normal subloop this is the preimage of the
centre `Z(L / N)` of the quotient loop under the quotient map `L → L / N`. -/
def centerMod (N : Set L) : Set L :=
  {a | ∀ x y : L, CongrMod N (a * x) (x * a) ∧
    CongrMod N (a * x * y) (a * (x * y)) ∧
    CongrMod N (x * a * y) (x * (a * y)) ∧
    CongrMod N (x * y * a) (x * (y * a))}

/-- The centre of the loop `L`: the elements that commute with every element and associate
with every pair of elements in every position, i.e. the intersection of the nucleus with the
commutant. -/
def center (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Set L :=
  {a | ∀ x y : L, a * x = x * a ∧ a * x * y = a * (x * y) ∧
    x * a * y = x * (a * y) ∧ x * y * a = x * (y * a)}

/-- The upper central series of the loop `L`: `Z₀ = {1}` and `Z_{n+1} / Z_n = Z(L / Z_n)`. -/
def upperCentralSeries (L : Type*) [Loop L] : ℕ → Set L
  | 0 => {1}
  | n + 1 => centerMod (upperCentralSeries L n)

/-- A loop is centrally nilpotent (in the sense of Bruck) if its upper central series reaches
the whole loop after finitely many steps. -/
def IsCentrallyNilpotent (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, upperCentralSeries L n = Set.univ

/-- In a loop, `a ⧵ b` is the unique solution of `a * x = b`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem eq_ldiv_of_mul_eq {a b x : L} (h : a * x = b) : x = a ⧵ b := by
  rw [← h, Loop.ldiv_mul]

/-- In a loop, `a / b` is the unique solution of `y * b = a`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem eq_rdiv_of_mul_eq {a b y : L} (h : y * b = a) : y = a / b := by
  rw [← h, Loop.mul_rdiv]

/-- Congruence modulo the trivial subloop is equality. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem congrMod_singleton_one (a b : L) : CongrMod {1} a b ↔ a = b := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl, rfl⟩
    exact Loop.mul_one b
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨1, rfl, (Loop.mul_one a).symm⟩

/-- The first term of the upper central series is the centre. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem upperCentralSeries_one : upperCentralSeries L 1 = center L := by
  ext a
  simp [upperCentralSeries, centerMod, center, congrMod_singleton_one]

end Loop

instance : Loop Unit where
  mul _ _ := ()
  one := ()
  div _ _ := ()
  ldiv _ _ := ()
  one_mul _ := rfl
  mul_one _ := rfl
  mul_ldiv _ _ := rfl
  ldiv_mul _ _ := rfl
  rdiv_mul _ _ := rfl
  mul_rdiv _ _ := rfl

/-- The trivial loop is centrally nilpotent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.isCentrallyNilpotent_unit : Loop.IsCentrallyNilpotent Unit :=
  ⟨0, Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The laws of the trivial loop have the finite basis `{x₀ ≈ x₁}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem LoopSignature.hasFiniteBasis_unit : LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis Unit := by
  refine ⟨{(.var 0, .var 1)}, Set.finite_singleton _,
    fun e => ⟨fun _ _ => rfl, fun _ β _ hS v => ?_⟩⟩
  have : ∀ a b : β, a = b := fun a b => hS _ rfl fun n => if n = 0 then a else b
  exact this _ _

/--
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

That is, there is a finite loop $L$ which is centrally nilpotent (its upper central series
reaches $L$) and whose laws, i.e. the identities in the loop signature `(*, ⧵, /, 1)` holding
in $L$, are not the equational consequences of any finite set of identities.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.4» :
    ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Loop L), Finite L ∧ Loop.IsCentrallyNilpotent L ∧
      ¬ LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis L := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.4»

items: The imperative 'Construct ...' is rendered as a plain existence statement `∃ (L : Type) (_ : Loop L), ...` (as in the repo's SteinerSystem 'Construct an S(t,k,n)' precedent) rather than `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ...`; the mathematical content is identical, and a negative resolution would be recorded by negating the statement.

Laws are taken in the full loop signature (*, ⧵, /, 1), the signature in which loops form a variety (standard in loop theory / universal algebra). Finite basedness is invariant under the term-equivalent (*, ⧵, /) signature.

Equational consequence is semantic, over all algebras of the loop signature (not just loops) living in `Type`. This is equivalent to syntactic derivability (Birkhoff) and to the relative notion 'finitely based within the variety of loops' since the loop axioms are finitely many identities; documented in the module docstring.
HasFiniteBasis is `∃ finite S, ∀ e, IsConsequence S e ↔ e ∈ laws L` (consequences of S are exactly the laws of L), which is the standard definition and implies S ⊆ laws L.

Upper central series is defined on `Set L` without constructing quotient loops: Z_{n+1} = {a | ∀ x y, (ax) ≡ (xa), ((ax)y) ≡ (a(xy)), ((xa)y) ≡ (x(ay)), ((xy)a) ≡ (x(ya)) mod Z_n} with u ≡ v mod N iff u ∈ vN. This coincides with the preimage of Z(L/Z_n) because each Z_n is (provably) a normal subloop and the quotient map is a surjective homomorphism; the check Z_1 = center is proved as an API lemma.
Central nilpotency is `∃ n, Z_n = univ` (class unrestricted); the trivial loop and finite groups (viewed as loops) are finitely based, so they are not degenerate witnesses.
Right division reuses Mathlib's `Div` class (`a / b` with `(a / b) * b = a`); left division is a new field with local notation `⧵`.

reviewer_notes: Statement is imperative ('Construct …'); following the repo precedent for construct-type problems (Wikipedia/SteinerSystem) and the decomposition note, it is stated as a plain existence theorem rather than `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ …` (only c05 used the latter; either is defensible, but CONTRIBUTING prefers plain `P` for non-questions). Modeling points a reviewer may want to confirm: (1) laws are taken in the full loop signature (1,·,\,/) with ℕ-indexed variables — the standard setting, and for finite loops term-equivalent to the (·)-only signature, so finite basedness is unaffected; (2) equational consequence is semantic over all algebras of the signature in universe `Type` — equivalent to derivability by Birkhoff completeness, and the universe restriction is harmless (countable free algebras give counter-models); consequence over all algebras vs over loops only is equivalent since the loop axioms are finitely many laws of L; (3) nilpotency is Bruck's central nilpotency via the upper central series, defined without quotients using cosets — this matches Z_{n+1}/Z_n = Z(L/Z_n) because each Z_n is a normal subloop (Bruck). Candidates c01/c02/c04/c07/c08 encode nilpotency instead as existence of a finite central series of congruences, and c01/c04 use syntactic equational derivability; all are equivalent, and their omission is a quality choice, not a faithfulness verdict.
